subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

items.prompt:
Newton's Third Law says forces come in pairs that are:
A) Equal and opposite
B) Always unequal
C) In the same direction
D) Zero

steps: Action and reaction forces are equal in size and opposite in direction.

items.prompt:
If object A pushes object B with 15 N, object B pushes A with:
A) 0 N
B) 15 N in the opposite direction
C) 30 N
D) 15 N in the same direction
items.answer: B) 15 N in the opposite direction

steps: The reaction force is equal and opposite.

items.prompt:
A swimmer pushes water backward and moves:
A) Backward
B) Forward
C) Nowhere
D) Downward only

steps: The water pushes the swimmer forward, the reaction force.

items.prompt:
Two cars of equal mass collide head-on. The forces they exert on each other are:
A) Larger on the faster car
B) Equal in size and opposite in direction
C) Only on one car
D) Zero
items.answer: B) Equal in size and opposite in direction

steps: Collision forces are an equal, opposite pair.

items.prompt:
How does an air bag reduce the force on a passenger?
A) It increases the stopping time
B) It makes the stop instant
C) It adds mass
D) It removes the collision
items.answer: A) It increases the stopping time

steps: Extending the stopping time reduces the force felt.

items.prompt:
A rocket pushes gas downward. What makes the rocket go up?
A) Gravity
B) The gas pushing the rocket up with an equal, opposite force
C) The air ahead
D) Nothing
items.answer: B) The gas pushing the rocket up with an equal, opposite force

steps: The reaction force on the rocket pushes it upward.

items.prompt:
Why don't the equal and opposite forces in a collision cancel to zero motion?
A) They act on different objects
B) They are not really equal
C) One force is fake
D) Motion is impossible
items.answer: A) They act on different objects

steps: Each force acts on a different object, so they do not cancel.

items.prompt:
An engineer wants to reduce the force on drivers in a crash. The best approach is to design the car to:
A) Stop as fast as possible
B) Extend the collision time with crumple zones
C) Be perfectly rigid
D) Increase the speed
items.answer: B) Extend the collision time with crumple zones

steps: Extending the collision time lowers the peak force.
